pages.identityNotes:
ONE PAGE, SEVEN TABS — the Audit Rules precedent, settled on the two stated tiebreakers and agreed by all six sweeps.

LEFT-MENU TEST. A corpus-wide census `grep -rhoP "[A-Z][A-Za-z &/-]{2,40}\(left menu\)"` over both guide dirs (1,859 files) returns 30 distinct labels. Workflows scores 8 (6 x 'Workflows (left menu)' + 2 x 'Click Workflows (left menu)'), second only to Forms and Fields. 'Approval Statuses', 'Authorized Approvers', 'Email Notifications', 'Workflow Settings', 'Confirmation Agreements', 'Reason Category and Codes', 'Purchase Request Settings' and 'Purchase Order Settings' score ZERO between them. `"Steps tab"` returns ZERO corpus-wide, so Steps is a wizard page and not a tab.

ROLE-GATE TEST. One gate for the whole surface, stated TWICE, verbatim, as 'permissions for the Workflows SECTION in Administration' — never per tab. This is the opposite of the Forms and Fields situation, where the Capture Processing Admin twin had a stricter gate of its own.

RELEASE-NOTE STRUCTURE [labelled: release note, cited for page NAME and STRUCTURE only]. updated-read-only-access-for-invoice-configuration-administrator-restricted-role-6df11845.md is organised under four headings — 'Forms and Fields Page', 'Group Configurations Page', 'Policies Page', 'Workflows Page' — the first three already pages in the graph. Under the fourth: 'View the list of Workflows and click on each item to view General, Steps, and Step Rules details', 'View the Approval Statuses and click on each item to view status details', 'View the workflow Settings'. One page containing all three, and General/Steps/Step Rules explicitly described as DETAILS OF A LIST ITEM, not pages.

THE SEVEN TABS, each with a verified click path from inside Workflows: Workflows, Settings, Email Notifications, Approval Statuses, Authorized Approvers, Confirmation Agreements, Reason Category and Codes. Two carry SUB-TABS: Approval Statuses > {Invoice, Purchase Request}; Authorized Approvers > {Configuration, Authorized Approver List}. Corroborated by understand-ad-hoc-steps-ce0af3e7.md ('on the Configuration tab of the Authorized Approvers tab').

PAGE vs OBJECT, kept apart. The page LISTS and EDITS workflow objects; a workflow is an object and there can be many. Both create-a-new-workflow files are about the OBJECT and were diffed by loio — genuinely two topics, NOT a gerund/imperative republish: 15992497 (2,017 B, loio 1599249793e440e794e4293a73dc68b4) is the conceptual note; 554e86aa (14,383 B, loio 554e86aad4494ef2b3af767ea746e15f) is the full General-page field procedure. 15992497 carries the only nested nav phrasing in the corpus: 'the General page in the Workflows tab of the Workflows tool'. The wizard General -> Steps -> Step Rules returns you to the tab ('When done with all rules and actions, click Done on the Workflows tab.') — the giveaway that it is a modal sequence, not navigation.

THE FOUR workflow-guides-*.md FILES, DIFFED AS INSTRUCTED: four distinct loio, four distinct body md5 (93fa7bbfd6 / 1ad7eaa05e / 1f30c5b2b4 / e052eac989), identical 4-row payload listing four EXTERNAL setup guides ('Refer to these guides when configuring and maintaining workflows.'). They are why this area LOOKS like four pages — SAP split the DOCUMENTATION by topic, not the UI. No node.

CONTRADICTIONS RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED. C1 Settings: 'Settings tab' vs 'Settings section of the Workflows tool' vs 'Settings page' vs 'Workflow Settings page' — tab wins because only the tab reading carries a click path. C2 Authorized Approvers: 'Authorized Approvers tab' (plural, 3 click paths) vs 'Authorized Approver tab' (singular, 2 paths) vs 'the Workflows, Authorized Approvers page' vs 'Authorized Approvers section' vs 'Add Authorized Approvers page within Workflows' — five labels, one surface, all paths land inside Workflows. C3 'Workflows tab' (14 topics) vs 'Workflow tab' (1). C4 'Email Notifications tab' vs singular. C5 'Confirmation Agreements tab' (the click step) vs 'Confirmation Agreement tab' (title and prose). C6 wizard vocabulary: General page / General step / Edit Workflow page; Add Workflow Step page vs window; Modify Workflow Step vs Steps window. C7 DEPTH COLLAPSE: administrator-experience-8b302852.md and approve-forward-feature-b847d65b.md put General-page fields 'on the Workflows page' — the ancestor; do NOT create a second node. C8 NAV DEPTH: 5 topics use the Invoice Processing Admin middle node, 8 omit it — abbreviation per the brief's own rule, both recorded, automation should try the middle node first.

C9 — THE ROLE-GATE CONTRADICTION, UNRESOLVED AND THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE FOR THE AUTOMATION. creating-a-reason-code-b2b61596.md says the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role IS REQUIRED to use the options on the Reason Category and Codes tab, then walks through New -> Save. The July 2025 release note says that same role has READ-ONLY access to Workflows with New/Copy/Remove disabled, and its enumeration covers only three of the seven tabs. Either that tab is carved out of the read-only rule or one statement is stale. I cannot settle it from the corpus. If the automation ever hits a permission wall on Workflows, this tab is the likely cause.

WHY REASON CATEGORY AND CODES IS STILL A TAB (the closest call in the group, and two sweeps rated it only 'medium'): it is the ONE surface here with a role gate different from the page's, and the brief's tiebreaker says own left-menu entry OR own role gate = page. Half the tiebreaker fires. Against it: zero left-menu hits, zero independent click paths, the gate sentence is explicitly tab-scoped ('the options on this tab'), and the Workflows guide's own revision history lists it as a tab beside Confirmation Agreements ('Reason Category and Codes tab and options'). Forms and Fields needed TWO ENTRY POINTS; this has none. Verdict: tab, with C9 attached.

BOUNDARY AGAINST BUILT PAGES, checked field by field. Routing Configuration (10 fields, all hierarchy-mapping import/search mechanics) — nothing in the Workflows tree duplicates it; no mis-homed field found; no finding raised against the graph on that axis. Audit Rules (91 fields) — REAL OVERLAP that is duplication, not new pages: the condition editor is explicitly shared ('The Condition page in the Workflows tool is similar to the Condition Editor page used in the Audit Rules tool'), so dedupe the Step Rules condition roster before extracting. Exceptions (8 fields) — the documented hub ('appear as options for the Audit Rules tool and Workflows tool when creating rules'); its LEVELS are consumed by three Workflows surfaces (Settings-tab thresholds, Authorized Approvers > Configuration Min/Max Exception Level, the Step Rules 'generate an exception' action) — all consumption, no new page. Invoice Settings (13 fields) — label collision only; NOTHING MOVES. Purchase Order Matching Rules (33 fields) carries confirmation_type / edit_confirmation_button from Receipt Confirmation Type, a DIFFERENT feature from workflow Confirmation Agreements — do not merge. Capture Processing Admin's Email Administration / Supplier Email Administration tabs are inbound image-capture aliases, not workflow notification surfaces.

roster.splitProposal:
SPLIT INTO TWO RUNS. Measured inventories (real `wc -c`), with overlaps computed by `comm`:

  Workflows               84 files   217,634 B   ~100 est. fields   (shares 2 files with Feature Hierarchies, 1 with Delegate Configurations)
  Feature Hierarchies     12 files    23,239 B     ~5 est. fields    (shares 2 files with Workflows)
  Email Reminders         17 files    37,033 B    ~25 est. fields    (shares nothing)
  Delegate Configurations 17 files    33,041 B    ~25 est. fields    (shares 1 file with Workflows)

RUN A — "Workflows" + "Feature Hierarchies". 94 unique files, 234,519 B, ~105 estimated fields.
They are paired for the stated reason: THEY SHARE SOURCE FILES — step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md and understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md, the second of which is a 69-row long catalog that two separate runs would otherwise read twice. Feature Hierarchies adds almost no cost (~5 fields, zero tables, zero raw-HTML) and it carries the Workflows build's hard forward reference ('You must define the authorized approver hierarchy (Invoice > Feature Hierarchies)'), so building them together also keeps that prerequisite edge inside one run's head.

RUN B (merged with --patch) — "Email Reminders" + "Delegate Configurations". 34 unique files, 70,074 B, ~50 estimated fields. Zero overlap with each other; exactly ONE 1,284 B file shared with Run A (delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md), whose field belongs to the WORKFLOWS General page — RUN B MUST NOT EXTRACT IT. Both are structurally simple: an object list plus an editor, two tabs each, no raw HTML tables.

THE IMBALANCE IS IRREDUCIBLE AND I AM NOT GOING TO PRETEND OTHERWISE. Run A is roughly 70/30 by bytes and 2:1 by estimated fields. That is not a cutting error — Workflows is a SINGLE INDIVISIBLE page holding about two thirds of the group's material (more than the built Audit Rules page's 91 fields), and because --patch REPLACES a page's fields wholesale, a split can never cut through it. Give Run A the stronger model tier and budget for a page with seven tabs, four sub-tabs, a three-page wizard and roughly a dozen dialogs, three of whose source files hide payload in raw HTML. Run B can run cheaper.

IF A THREE-WAY SPLIT IS PREFERRED, the only clean cut is {Workflows + Feature Hierarchies} / {Email Reminders} / {Delegate Configurations} — but it buys nothing, because the binding constraint is Workflows and not the tail.

DO NOT split Feature Hierarchies away from Workflows into Run B: it would duplicate the shared long catalog and separate the prerequisite from its consumer. DO NOT attempt to split Workflows by tab: --patch would overwrite the first half's fields.

pagehood.verdict: ENDORSE THE FOUR-PAGE ROSTER — no page added, removed, merged or split. I attacked each on click-path, role gate, graph collision and census, and every structural claim reproduced, several to the byte: all 144 sourceQuotes verify with grep -F (0 misses); the left-menu census returns 30 distinct labels with Workflows=8 and every candidate tab=0; "Steps tab"=0 corpus-wide; tools-guides hits for Workflows tool/page/tab=0; totalBytes exact on all four pages (217,634 / 37,033 / 33,041 / 23,239); rawTableFiles=3 exact; split arithmetic exact (Run A 94/234,519, Run B 34/70,074, overlaps 2/1/0). I also censused every "<Label> tab" string corpus-wide hunting an eighth Workflows tab and found none — the remainder all home to already-built pages. All five inherited verdicts are sound, settled with commands not plausibility, and I STRENGTHENED finding (1): the Workflows guide's own revision history (general-information-8b3b0308.md:299) names "Filter invoice items..." and "Allow processor to recall an invoice..." as "Addition of two new options to the Settings tab", and those two strings appear nowhere else in the corpus except rows 4-5 of the packed raw <table> in invoice-settings-cace748d.md — direct proof the invoice member sits on Workflows > Settings tab, which the roster had only indirectly. severeFindings.title: tools-guides is written off by a phrasing test, not by content — the 'admin-guides only' instruction is over-broad
severeFindings.detail: The roster ran `grep -rl -e "Workflows tool" -e "Workflows page" -e "Workflows tab"` over the 650 tools-guides files, got ZERO (I reproduced it), and concluded 'aim the build at admin-guides only.' severeFindings.title: The Delegate Configurations 'two user interfaces' UI hint is 2014 boilerplate present in 40 files
severeFindings.detail: The roster records: "delegate-configuration-8b2bd26d.md's revision history records 'added information about two user interfaces', which is a UI-variant HINT with no accompanying variant topic — record it, do not act on it." `grep -rn "two user interfaces"` over both guide dirs returns 40 FILES, including audit-rules-8b297db8.md, policies-8b34cecf.md, forms-and-fields-8b2e66f6.md, invoice-settings-8b345df1.md, routing-configuration-8b511516.md — i.e. most of the twenty already-built pages. It is a September 17, 2014 boilerplate revision-history line, not a page-specific signal. Recording it on one page and not the other thirty-nine invites a downstream builder to act on noise, and it is the same observation-vs-inference error the brief calibrates on.

severeFindings.title: The 13-attribution: a THIRD accounting fits the roster's own stated criterion better than its preferred one
severeFindings.detail: The roster offers two accountings and prefers 7 tabs + 3 wizard pages + 3 settings tables 'because it maps onto NAMED ARTEFACTS WITH THEIR OWN TOPIC TITLES'. My independent 'X page' census over the 120-file workflow superset returns: Approval Flow 13, Workflows 12, Steps 8, Step Rules 7, General 6, Settings 2, Authorized Approvers 2, Edit Workflow 1, Condition Editor 1. A third accounting therefore also reaches thirteen — 7 tabs + General + Steps + Step Rules + The Condition Page + Edit Condition window + Edit Action window — and The Condition Page has its OWN TOPIC TITLE three times over (the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md, the-condition-page-3408dec8.md, conditional-expressions-and-the-condition-page-4d98af34.md), whereas Invoice/Purchase Request/Purchase Order Settings are the members the roster has to argue are page-like. This does NOT change the page count and does not weaken the one-page verdict, which I could not break: my tab census over 95 workflow-domain files returns exactly the seven tabs, exactly four sub-tabs and one historical rename (Payment Request Approval Statuses), with no eighth. It weakens only the confidence with which the reconciliation picks a winner.
severeFindings.action: Add the third accounting to the reconciliation and state that three accountings now reach thirteen and the corpus cannot choose between them — rather than presenting one as the best fit for the stated criterion.

completeness.verdict: The roster's page count, its one-page/seven-tab verdict, and its hardest calls all survive adversarial attack. I reproduced every load-bearing mechanical claim: the Finding (1) clincher (0/2 on "select their own approver"; `grep -rl "apply globally to"` returns exactly the three family files; "Type a number from one to 99." returns 1 in each; cace748d `<tr`=3 `<p`=6), the left-menu census (30 labels — and I added the calibration the roster omitted: all 60 raw "(left menu)" occurrences are accounted for by those 30, so nothing is hidden), the graph string counts (Approval Statuses 0, Email Notifications 0, Authorized Approver 0, Step Rules 0, Workflows 36), the New Experience census (5 filename hits, 9 content hits, none workflow config), the raw <table> census (3 real tables in the workflow domain, all 3 seeded; the 4th is Print Condition Rules), and 16 spot-checked sourceQuotes, all verbatim. The deliberate exclusion of the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md (11,176 B, the domain's 3rd-largest file) is CORRECT — it already sources 16 built Audit Rules fields. Workflows' seed list covers the entire top ten by bytes; no stub-aiming there. The failures are all failures of REACH, not judgement, and there are nine. The most consequential: a documented admin surface (Authorized Approval Limits, 6,917 B across two admin-guides files, own click path, own role gate, seven named fields) rejected on a false claim that the corpus defers it externally — leaving the per-user approval limit with no home anywhere; a Group Configurations overview seeded on Feature Hierarchies, the thinnest page in the group, risking re-homing of built G1 fields; four documented General-page timeout fields recorded as homeless; and a uiVariant verdict that is backwards — a dated 2025-09-19 line says the Workflows topics were rewritten to the new UI in place, so the missing twin is a replacement, not a gap. That last one I nominate as a SIXTH inherited finding: it is the only ambiguity that, if wrong, invalidates every navPath in the group simultaneously. Split verdict: keep the two-run shape (it does not cut through a page, so --patch is safe), but Authorized Approval Limits must go in Run A because it shares the limit-definition topics with the Authorized Approvers tab, which makes Run A's irreducible imbalance slightly worse. Out-of-scope surfaces surfaced and reported so they are not lost: Vendor Manager (5 unresolved endpoints), Print Condition Rules (a real <table> and a List page), Vendor Handling, Form Types, and details-section-49500221.md (29,059 B / 1,360 rows, uncited, import-extract domain). One correction to my own work is recorded in the file rather than deleted: I first called the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md uncited; the graph references it 4 times and Group 5 already owns its Level value set, so it is a dedupe reference, not unread material.
